trust_decision.summary: At the pinned commit nothing decides whether a transitive external reference may be fetched: Settings.forbid_external exists (default True) but is never read anywhere in src, so every http/https URL reached via xsd:import, xsd:include, wsdl:import or lxml entity resolution is handed straight to Transport.load; the fix creates the decision in load_external/ImportResolver and keeps the user-supplied entry-point document exempt via a new _initial flag.

landing_point.why: The report is 'SSRF while loading a WSDL'; load_external is the single function that turns a schemaLocation/import location into transport.load(url), and xsd:import, xsd:include and wsdl:import all funnel into it.

fix_sites.entry_point: every caller of the blocked fetch: zeep.Client(...), zeep.xsd.Schema(...), zeep.loader.load_external(...)
zeep.loader.parse_xml, i.e. any document parsed by Client / Schema (lxml entity and DTD resolution)
zeep.loader.parse_xml, reached from Client response parsing and from every document load
zeep.Settings.forbid_external default, consumed by every Client(...) / Schema(...) construction
zeep.Client(wsdl_url) and python -m zeep URL (entry-point document must stay loadable)
wsdl:import inside a document loaded by zeep.Client(wsdl_url)
zeep.xsd.Schema.add_document_by_url(url) and the soap-encoding auto-import route

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The setting already exists with a documented default, so the check can be added at the sink and the default value in settings.py (plus the entry-point exemption it implies) dismissed as a backwards-compatibility matter that has nothing to do with the reported SSRF.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The URL the user passes to Client()/Schema.add_document_by_url must still be fetched when forbid_external is enabled, and the setting must stay permissive by default: a check placed before the initial-load distinction, or a default left at the pinned True, breaks every existing Client('http://...?wsdl') load and every test that builds a client from a remote-looking URL.

O6_input_shapes: relative schemaLocation/schemaLocation-less import resolved against base_url before the scheme test (src/zeep/loader.py:87-89)
absolute http:// URL through xsd:import / xsd:include (src/zeep/xsd/visitor.py:238)
lxml entity/DTD resolution through the parser resolver (src/zeep/loader.py:18-21)
sync branch load_external and async branch load_external_async (src/zeep/loader.py:93-110)
file-like object passed as url, which skips the transport entirely (src/zeep/loader.py:84-85)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Inline <xs:schema> in a deserialized payload builds a nested Schema with a fresh default Settings(), so its xsd:import/xsd:include targets are fetched even when the client enabled forbid_external
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It is response deserialization of an inline schema, not loading the WSDL the report is about, and the nested Schema deliberately has its own settings object.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: zeep/xsd/elements plus zeep/xsd and zeep/wsdl/messages (the callers at wsdl/messages/soap.py:452)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: file:// and bare local-path import/include locations stay open: the new check only tests for http/https, while absolute_location keeps a file:// scheme and Transport.load maps file:// and schemeless paths to the local filesystem
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The advisory is SSRF over http/https, so reading a local file looks like a different weakness, and file:// support is a documented transport feature.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same loader file, plus zeep/transports.py (one package boundary)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second fetch helper (_retrieve_data) parallel to the wsdl document loader that calls load_external and could carry its own initial/not-initial policy
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: A maintainer adding another document kind (inline schema, xi:include, advice) would naturally route it through this visitor helper and repeat the flag handling by hand.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Nested Schema constructed from a node with the transport but no settings/source object, so the security setting silently reverts to its default
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This is exactly the shape a maintainer writes when a schema is discovered while parsing a value rather than loaded from a URL: the location and settings are simply not at hand.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Response XML parsed through parse_xml with a per-request transport, a second parser instantiation that must inherit the same resolver policy
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The response path is written separately from the document path and receives client.settings only, so a future resolver hook would be added here too.

O9_family: Server-side request forgery through external XML reference resolution (CWE-918)

O10_build.toolchain: setuptools via pyproject.toml (build-backend setuptools.build_meta); pip install -e '.[test]'; pytest 8.3.3 with requests_mock, pytest-httpx, pytest-asyncio
O10_build.project_tests: tests/test_loader.py, tests/test_xsd_schemas.py, tests/test_wsdl.py and tests/test_settings.py; tests/utils.py:32-43 provides DummyTransport, a dict-backed transport, so document/import fetch behaviour is testable without a socket

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add 'if settings.forbid_external: raise ExternalReferenceForbidden(url)' at the top of load_external (or in Transport.load) - with the pinned default True that blocks the user's own WSDL/schema URL and breaks every Client(url) load.
